about: The tract of the Annunciation of the Blessed Virgin Mary in the 1962 Roman Missal.

s01.translation: Hear, daughter, and see, and incline your ear, for the King has desired your beauty. All the wealthy among the people will seek your favor; kings’ daughters in your honor. Virgins will be brought to the King, following her; her closest companions will be brought to you. They will be brought with joy and exultation; they will be brought into the temple of the King.

w040.explanation: The literal image is to entreat your face or countenance: in this setting the rich seek your favor.

w044.explanation: The Latin gives a nominal phrase, daughters of kings in your honor, without a finite verb.

w054.explanation: The feminine plural refers to the women close to her in the bridal procession, hence her companions. The form is grammatically superlative.

w057.explanation: The address can turn from the bride to the King. The Latin pronoun itself does not identify the addressee by gender.
